scene: Episode 02 · INSERT REEL 2 — the cold-open hook and two macro inserts
shot: Three separate 10s inserts cut in camera, to be split in Resolve: C1 HOOK — a passenger borrows the frozen man's sugar at breakfast (opens the episode) · C2 Beatrice's hand rimes on the counter (Sc15 button) · C3 Amina writes KELL under PASSENGERS (Sc14 payoff of the Sc03 plant).
prompt:
Live-action mythic modernism. Photoreal, tactile, cinematic, anamorphic widescreen, 24fps, shallow depth of field. THREE SHOTS, cut in camera at the stated times, and no other coverage. All spoken dialogue is in ENGLISH.

THIS FILM IS THREE SEPARATE INSERT SHOTS FOR AN EDIT, IN THREE DIFFERENT PLACES. NOTHING AND NOBODY CARRIES OVER FROM ONE SHOT TO THE NEXT.

REFERENCE PRECEDENCE: @Image1 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR SHOT 1 — the warm, occupied walnut first-class carriage with the frozen white man at his RIGHT-HAND WINDOW TABLE. @Image2 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THAT MAN in Shot 1: his face, his PALE GREY-OATMEAL OVERCOAT and his frozen state, which is correct for this shot. @Image3 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE TIMBER BOOTH in Shot 2. @Image4 and @Image5 are the authority for BEATRICE'S SLEEVE AND HAND in Shot 2, and @Image5 for THE RIME ON THE BACK OF HER HAND. @Image6 IS THE ABSOLUTE AUTHORITY FOR THE NOTEBOOK PAGE in Shot 3 — its hand-drawn columns and the last column headed PASSENGERS. @Image7 is the authority for AMINA'S SLATE-BLUE SLEEVE AND GLOVED HAND in Shot 3.

=== SHOT 1 — 0:00 to 0:10 — C1 · THE HOOK · WIDE TO MEDIUM, 32mm, SLOW DOLLY DOWN THE AISLE ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
A PASSENGER (a well-dressed woman, cheerful, absent-minded, to the frozen man): "Thank you."
ANNOUNCEMENT (a calm, warm, exact railway voice over the carriage speakers): "The Hessel crossing is warm and will remain warm. Passengers are thanked for their continued regard."

Breakfast service in a warm, busy, first-class walnut saloon carriage at 3200K: passengers at every table, a porter pouring tea, steam rising from cups and teapots, cutlery, folded newspapers, low warm lamps, clear dry windows onto a white frozen lake. Some passengers are quietly impossible — long pointed ears and olive-grey skin at one table, a very tall thin traveller whose hands are wrapped in paper labels at another — and nobody remarks on them.
THE MOVE: the camera travels slowly and continuously down the aisle at seated-eye height, past a passenger's shoulder close to the lens, toward the RIGHT-HAND WINDOW TABLE.
AT THAT TABLE SITS A MAN WHO IS FROZEN SOLID — exactly @Image2: upright, chalk-white skin, his PALE GREY-OATMEAL COAT stiff, A STARBURST OF WHITE RIME RADIATING OUTWARD FROM HIS STERNUM across his lapels, both hands flat on the cloth. HE IS COMPLETELY MOTIONLESS. His teapot beside him is STILL STEAMING. The window beside him is clear and dry. NOBODY IN THE CARRIAGE LOOKS AT HIM.
AS THE CAMERA ARRIVES, A PASSENGER AT THE NEXT TABLE LEANS ACROSS WITHOUT LOOKING AT HIM, TAKES THE LITTLE SUGAR BOWL FROM HIS TABLE, says her two words to him pleasantly, and goes back to her breakfast. He does not move. The announcement plays over the end of the shot.
SOUND: the warm hum of the carriage, cutlery, cups, low conversation. ALL BACKGROUND VOICES ARE LOW AND COMPLETELY INDISTINCT AND NO WORD IN THEM CAN BE MADE OUT; only the named lines in this film are intelligible. NO music.

CUT at 0:10.

=== SHOT 2 — 0:10 to 0:20 — C2 · MACRO, 100mm, LOCKED · THE MANIFEST BOOTH · BEATRICE'S HAND ===
NOBODY SPEAKS IN THIS SHOT.

Extreme close-up on a worn timber counter inside a cramped wooden booth, lit by ONE HARD LOW WARM BULB raking across it. A cream form with a fresh ink signature lies on the counter. A WOMAN'S RIGHT HAND — the cuff of a BLACK WRAP-COAT sleeve at the wrist — lays a pen down beside the form and then rests flat and still on the timber.
ACROSS THE SHOT, FINE WHITE RIME GROWS OUTWARD FROM HER KNUCKLES in delicate needles across the backs of her fingers, exactly like @Image5 — the same outward frost as on the frozen man — while the hand itself stays relaxed and still. The frost throws its own tiny hard shadows under the warm bulb. The counter, the pen and the paper carry NO frost. The hand never reacts to it.
SOUND: wind outside the hatch; the bulb's faint tick; a rubber stamp being put away off screen. No music.

CUT at 0:20.

=== SHOT 3 — 0:20 to 0:30 — C3 · MACRO, 100mm, LOCKED · AMINA'S NOTEBOOK ===
NOBODY SPEAKS IN THIS SHOT.

Extreme close-up of AMINA'S OPEN FIELD NOTEBOOK, exactly @Image6: hand-drawn ruled columns densely filled with pencil figures, and the LAST COLUMN, headed PASSENGERS, EMPTY under its heading. Warm raking light across the paper. The heading PASSENGERS stays fully inside the frame for the whole shot; the camera does not move and only the pencil moves.
HER PENCIL ENTERS — her gloved hand and SLATE-BLUE sleeve at the edge of frame — and, under the heading PASSENGERS, in neat small pencil capitals, WRITES ONE WORD OF FOUR LETTERS: K, E, L, L. Then the pencil lifts and rests on the page beside the word. The word KELL sits alone in the column that was empty.
SOUND: graphite on paper; wind beyond a stone doorway. No music.

Pronounce these words exactly and clearly: HESSEL, CROSSING, CONTINUED, REGARD.

PALETTE: carriage amber #B8801F, walnut #4A3122, rime white #E9F1F4, bulb amber #B8801F, graphite #3A3733, paper bone #DED5C2.

FROST GROWS OUTWARD FROM BODIES AND NEVER INWARD FROM ANYTHING: it starts on a person's skin or clothes and its fine needles spread AWAY from them. The stone, the windows and the air never frost. Nothing glows anywhere except the lamps and the bulb. No machinery, no gears, no runes, no magical light, no lens flare, no particles, no smoke, no digital element, no screens, no interface, no signage, no ornament, and no Victorian, Edwardian, medieval or steampunk detail.
